assistant|recipe_suggestion: Caprese Salad: fresh mozzarella, juicy tomatoes, and basil leaves with olive oil and balsamic glaze
Thai Basil Chicken: stir-fried chicken with Thai basil, chilies, garlic, and lemongrass, served with rice or noodles
Pesto Pasta: basil blended with garlic, pine nuts, Parmesan, olive oil, tossed with linguine, cherry tomatoes, grilled chicken
Basil and Lemon Spaghetti: basil, lemon zest, garlic, and olive oil as a light spaghetti sauce
Indian-Style Basil Chutney: basil blended with cilantro, green chilies, ginger, and lemon juice
Mint Chutney: mint-based cooling chutney used as a dip or sauce for grilled meats or vegetables
Minty Fresh Salad: mint leaves with feta, cucumbers, cherry tomatoes, lemon juice, and olive oil
Mint Julep: cocktail made with bourbon, mint leaves, sugar, and crushed ice
Grilled Lamb with Mint Sauce: lamb chops marinated in olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, and mint, then grilled
Minty Yogurt Sauce: mint leaves with yogurt, cucumber, garlic, and dill, served with grilled meats or as a dip
Herby Lemonade: lemonade infused with fresh basil and mint leaves for a summer drink
Middle Eastern-Style Salad: basil and mint with bulgur, cherry tomatoes, cucumbers, feta, and lemon-tahini dressing
Basil and Mint Chimichurri: basil, mint, parsley, garlic, red pepper flakes, red wine vinegar, and olive oil blended into an Argentinean herb sauce
Thai-Style Basil and Mint Stir-Fry: chicken or tofu stir-fried with Thai basil, mint, chilies, and lemongrass, served with rice or noodles
Basil and Mint Infused Water: fresh basil and mint leaves added to a pitcher of water
assistant|companion_plant_suggestion: Basil is a good companion plant for tomatoes, repelling whiteflies and aphids
Marigold is a good companion plant for tomatoes, repelling nematodes and attracting beneficial insects
Borage is a good companion plant for tomatoes, attracting bees and butterflies for pollination and providing shade and support
Chives are a good companion plant for tomatoes, naturally repelling aphids and other pests
Oregano is a good companion plant for tomatoes, acting as a natural fungicide against early blight and septoria leaf spot
Parsley is a good companion plant for tomatoes, repelling carrot flies and other pests
Carrots are a good companion plant for tomatoes, breaking up compacted soil and improving structure for tomato roots
Radish is a good companion plant for tomatoes, repelling cucumber beetles that spread bacterial wilt
Dill is a good companion plant for tomatoes, repelling aphids, spider mites, and other pests
Comfrey is a good companion plant for tomatoes, acting as a fertilizer and bringing up nutrients from the subsoil
Nasturtium is a good companion plant for cherry tomatoes, repelling aphids, whiteflies, and other pests
assistant|companion_plant_warning: Fennel should not be planted near tomatoes because it inhibits tomato growth and flavor
Kohlrabi should not be planted near tomatoes because it attracts the same pests
Potatoes should not be planted near tomatoes because both are nightshades susceptible to similar diseases
Rue should not be planted near tomatoes because it can be toxic to them
assistant|gardening_tip: Plant companion plants around the perimeter of the cherry tomato bed to create a trap crop effect
Plant companion plants at the same time as or slightly before cherry tomatoes to give them a head start
Keep soil consistently moist and well-draining for cherry tomatoes and companion plants
assistant|pest_control_suggestion: Neem oil should be diluted with water, usually 2-4 teaspoons per quart, to control aphids
Spray neem oil on all plant surfaces including leaf undersides, stem joints, and flower buds where aphids concentrate
Apply neem oil every 7-10 days to maintain effectiveness against aphids
Avoid applying neem oil during peak sun hours; apply in early morning or evening to prevent plant damage
Mixing neem oil with mild dish soap can enhance effectiveness against aphids
Insecticidal soap can control aphids on pepper plants as a gentle, non-toxic pesticide
Horticultural oil, a refined mineral oil, can suffocate aphids on pepper plants
Ladybugs can be introduced to the garden as natural predators of aphids
Lacewings can be introduced to the garden as generalist predators that feed on aphids, whiteflies, and spider mites
Parasitic wasps such as Aphidius ervi can be introduced to control aphid populations
Hoverfly larvae feed on aphids and can help control populations
Fine-mesh screens or row covers can physically block aphids from reaching pepper plants
Pyrethrin, a natural pesticide from chrysanthemum flowers, can control aphids on pepper plants
Diatomaceous earth sprinkled around the base of pepper plants dehydrates and kills aphids
Planting aphid-resistant pepper varieties can help prevent infestations
Release ladybugs in large numbers, e.g. 1,000-2,000, to effectively control aphid populations
Release lacewing eggs or larvae near aphid-infested areas so the larvae feed on aphids
Provide pollen-rich flowers and sheltered areas to help ladybugs and lacewings thrive
Release natural predators when aphid populations are present but not too severe
Removing weeds regularly helps prevent aphid infestations since weeds harbor aphids
Improving air circulation and avoiding overwatering pepper plants helps prevent aphid infestations
assistant|pest_control_opinion: Believes introducing beneficial insects like ladybugs or lacewings is a great, natural, environmentally friendly idea for the user's garden
